speaker: Scottish Cup Semi Final
quote_text:
How do you reflect on that this afternoon?
Tough afternoon. And, um, of course not the result  what we wanted, but at the same time, if I reflect  
whole—whole 90 minutes, uh, we pretty much knew  how the game will go, you know, that they will  
come with relentless energy, they will try to get,  you know, McGregor as a number six to play more  
with the ball, to use the striker, uh, to drop the  ball and get the runners there. I think we—we did  
that. We stayed solid—what was it—30 minutes?  But then, as always, couple of not-as-good  
decisions with the balls and you make—make those  and, um, they can feel it, they can smell it,  
and they punish you. And that’s—that’s  what happened. And then at the halftime,  
the cup dream—it was gone. Only thing to play for  anymore was the pride. The pride to play for this  
beautiful club, play for our fans, and I think our  players second half—they went—they went there and,  
you know, they showed the character, they showed  that. But, uh, end of the day, congratulations to  
Celtic. They deserve it, of course, to go through  and no complaints about the result or anything.
You know, how much do those periods come down  to maybe concentration? Because, as you say,  
you show a fair bit of evidence that  you’re comfortable within the game,  
but then it obviously gets away very quickly.
Yeah, but, um, I would—I would use it other way  around. And I use the example of Celtic. The game  
is 5–0, 87 minutes played, they still do the same  things what they did, you know, the first five  
minutes. Still do the same things—same runs, ball  out, same there. We did 30 minutes things what we  
were practicing. Then we think, okay, let’s do  some—let’s try something different. And then,  
boom, everything goes—everything goes, you know,  out of our hands. And yes, we need to learn that,  
that we just need to be humble, patient enough,  just do, you know, the things what are working.
You don’t have one moment to  cheer initially—do you have  
any complaints about the goal being ruled out?
Uh, wow, I have not seen, you know, on  the video. Yes, there was some kind of,  
you know, shuffle, you know, when we win  the ball, you know, in a build-up. And,  
um, I feel a little bit for MacKenzie, you  know—it was beautiful strike, you know. So,  
so yeah, but that’s how it is. So, as I said,  it’s no complaints. And that was—what a fantastic  
cup journey we had. We deserved it to be in  this cup semi-final. We came here to compete,  
to give us chance to get the final. But  it didn’t happen this year. So, yes,  
we are sad, we suffer a little bit, but we  need to freshen up and go—go again tomorrow.
Simo, knowing at halftime that the tie was dead,  how important was it that players put on a good...  
didn’t get a really bad score in the second  half for the five games that are still to come?
Yes, exactly. Because only thing what we were  talking—the yes, football, tactical things always,  
because it’s a football. But we were talking about  this—that we need to show what kind of team we  
are. Because you could show easily to collapse and  they could go and go and kill you even, you know,  
worse. But the players showed it. And it was,  as I said, there was not other choice than go  
out and show it what we are. Because first half we  didn’t do the things well enough to stay in this  
tie. And then the dream was gone. But the pride  was there, you know, to play for—for it. And I  
think the players showed—players showed, you know,  this—this, you know. And the players who came on,  
you know, it was good—good shift from them. You  know, they—they made me think a lot of things,  
you know, how we going to go, you  know, these last five matches.
You got 15 minutes into [Carey] as well?
Yeah. Yeah, we did it. And, you know, it was  good to see back. And especially, you know,  
for himself, it has been very, very tough. But  of course for the team as well. And we see what  
kind of player he is. And of course we need  to understand—one year without the football,  
two weeks team trainings—you cannot  be, you know, even close, you know,  
where you are. But now he’s healthy,  and let’s see that we get more and  
more training him inside to him. So I—I  believe he can—he can help us a lot.
Simo, did you see—like, did you see enough,  despite the scoreline in that second half,  
to make you believe that you can stay  in this league with those players?
Yeah, that—that’s the thing. You know, these  games are totally different. This was a cup—cup,  
cup, semi-final against top, top, top, top,  top opponent, you know. And, uh, as I—I can’t  
predict the future, but I can say only, you know,  we had, as I said it, very good cup journey. And  
these cup games between the league games—they  were like a breath of—of fresh air to us,  
out of this pressure of the Premiership. And it  was same today. This was the cup semi-final. Day  
to dream. Go and out and play. Now, tomorrow we  are back, you know, what means most to our club,  
to ourselves, you know, these Premiership games.  And, you know, I have—I’ve said it a long time,  
I see what my players can do it. But if we  use this game example, it’s still there,  
what it affects us. We can do a lot of good  things, but then our bad things are dragging  
us down. And they have been long time there. And  that’s the thing what we need to fix. If we can  
do that, I believe our level is good enough to  compete and, you know, to stay in this league.
Thank you.
Thank you.
title: Simo Valakari Post Match Press Conference | St Johnstone 0-5 Celtic - Scottish Cup Semi Final
